layers.name: base
layers.about: Helpers that name no subsystem, and the contracts shared outside the server. Open: every crate above may use them.

crates.name: droppen-base
crates.about: The clock, text codecs, private files, process guards, outbound webhooks, the environment, the program's name.

crates.name: droppen-search-path
crates.about: The PATH rule shared with the desktop app.

crates.name: rh-proto
crates.about: The cloud protocol, shared with the hub, the relays and the test device.

crates.name: droppen-plugin-sdk
crates.about: The plugin contract.

layers.name: platform
layers.about: What the subsystems stand on: the instance and its files, the HTTP kit, the pty shims, the supervisor. Open: every crate above may use them; inside the layer, each uses what its mayUse lists.

crates.name: droppen-instance
crates.about: The shared Paths, the instance's directories and lock, its identity, the databases.

crates.name: droppen-http
crates.about: Errors, extractors, response types, the OpenAPI helpers, the origin guard, the config.

crates.name: droppen-pty
crates.about: The pty shims that outlive the server.

crates.name: droppen-supervisor
crates.about: The supervising process and self-update.

crates.name: rh-client
crates.about: A device's side of the hub API.

layers.name: domain
layers.about: The subsystems. Each uses only the domain crates its mayUse lists: auth under files, workbench and plugins, all of them under sessions, sessions under accounts, accounts under notify and setup; the aggregator under the agent, both under cloud, and neither uses another subsystem.

crates.name: droppen-auth
crates.about: Users, logins, tickets, the Identity extractor.
notes: Asks for notify's caller capability through its NotifyCredential port, which the entry fills.

crates.name: droppen-files
crates.about: Home-directory access behind the path guard, and the media proxy.

crates.name: droppen-workbench
crates.about: Terminal and app panes, saved screens, UI preferences.

crates.name: droppen-plugins
crates.about: The plugin store, installs and serving.

crates.name: droppen-sessions
crates.about: The session vocabulary, stores, listing and attention; owns the Transcripts port.

crates.name: droppen-accounts
crates.about: The account store, rotation, the quota cache and sweep, limits; owns the Login port.

crates.name: droppen-notify
crates.about: Alert channels: Bark, Web Push and the alert fan-out.
notes: Answers droppen-auth's NotifyCredential port from the entry; its caller travels in droppen-http's NotifyGrant, which neither crate has to name the other for.

crates.name: droppen-setup
crates.about: The first-run guide, CLI detection and installs.

crates.name: droppen-aggregator
crates.about: The device role: copies of other machines; owns the Enrollment port.

crates.name: droppen-agent
crates.about: The machine role: link, chain, relays, direct path, streams, rotation; owns the StreamSource and LinkHost ports.

crates.name: droppen-cloud
crates.about: The Droppen-link routes, the remote-view gate and link control. The StreamSource the link copies sessions from is the entry's (stream_source), so cloud names no sessions code.

layers.name: providers
layers.about: The provider base, then what stands on it: the three implementations and drive, which do not see one another. Each lists the domain crates it may use. Nothing but the entry names an implementation.

crates.name: droppen-provider
crates.about: Provider, Run, Models, the registry, the spawn gate, the session shim, queue, receipts, questions, drafts.
notes: The base's own items: receipts and questions, drafts, the run journal (runs), and the spawn gate with its claims (gate).
shim, the session shim: Claude Code and Codex both start their CLI through it.

models keeps its routes and the list's wire types here; each provider's list is its own (droppen_provider_claude_code::models with its probe, droppen_provider_codex::models, droppen_provider_acp::models).

crates.name: droppen-provider-claude-code
crates.about: Claude Code: the resident driver, its transcripts, roots, readings, logins and recordings.

crates.name: droppen-provider-codex
crates.about: Codex: the app-server driver, its threads and tools, its quota and its login.

crates.name: droppen-provider-acp
crates.about: Every configured ACP agent, from data.

crates.name: droppen-drive
crates.about: Send, start and answer; the live and global feeds, search; chats; schedules.

layers.name: entry
layers.about: The binary: the router, AppState, the wiring, the command line. It may use every crate below it.

crates.name: remote-hand-server
crates.about: The router, the app, the web files, the desktop app's settings, shutdown, export and the binary.

sourceMatches.about: Matches of Source::Claude, Source::Codex or Source::Acp in code built outside tests, in every file under the server's and each workspace crate's `src`, the crates exempt names aside. Outside them Source is only the key that picks a provider, so the number may only go down. The server's source scans (provider_tests::gate) parse each file, count the matches and hold them to count; check-layers prints it. Three are Source::as_str's own arms in droppen-sessions, the wire names. Two stay on purpose: schedule's task_at reads a stored task's source by name ("codex" as Codex, anything else as Claude Code), because decoding it through the providers would put the provider registry into the task store.

exempt.why: Claude Code's provider: it answers for Source::Claude.
Codex's provider: it answers for Source::Codex.
The ACP agents' provider: it answers for Source::Acp.

outside.about: Workspace members that are not the server's crates: the relay, as a library and as its binary, and the developer kit. Each uses the crates of the open layers and the others outside, and no crate of the layers depends on one of them.

forbidden.name: the provider base names no implementation
forbidden.why: The provider base names no implementation: each registers itself on the base, and only the entry names one.

forbidden.name: the implementations and drive do not see one another
forbidden.why: The three implementations and drive stand side by side on the provider base and do not see one another.

forbidden.name: the domain is under the providers
forbidden.why: The providers stand on the domain, never the other way round: a domain crate that needs one declares a port, and the entry wires it.

forbidden.name: the transport carries no app
forbidden.why: The machine's transport carries no app: the agent and the aggregator use no other domain crate, only the agent the aggregator below it.

wrappers.why: A pseudo-terminal is droppen-pty's, with the shims that keep one alive across a restart; everything else opens one through it.

A websocket outside the routes axum serves is the link's: the hub and relay client, the agent's sockets to the hub, the relays and this server, the relay itself and the developer kit. Tests use it as a client as they like.
